from.place: proof: a section vanishing on the closed fibre over a valuation ring already vanishes modulo a nonzero element of the maximal ideal

title: Vanishing on the closed fibre over a valuation ring descends to some A/pi
statement: Let A be a valuation ring with maximal ideal \mathfrak m, assume A is not a field, let f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}(A) be of finite presentation [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], let X_0 be the closed fibre, let L be an invertible module on X [def-sc-invertible-module], and let s\in\Gamma(X,L) with s|_{X_0}=0. Then there is a nonzero \pi\in\mathfrak m such that s restricts to zero on X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}(A)}\operatorname{Spec}(A/\pi).

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma lemma-triviality-generic-fibre-valuation-ring, Tag 0EX8, proof sentence 'kappa = colim A/pi ... see Limits, Lemma limits-lemma-descend-section'

proof.text: On an affine open U, use the quotient-base-change ideal formula to identify the ideal of X times Spec(A/I) with the extension of I to Gamma(U,O_X). The closed-immersion unit quotient identifies the image of ideal multiplication with the kernel of its unit. Evaluating this kernel on U and applying the affine ideal-times-module sections calculation gives: the pullback unit kills t exactly when t belongs to (I Gamma(U,O_X)) Gamma(U,L). Compare the adjunction in the unit-quotient theorem with the canonical chosen adjunction using rightAdjointUniq; its component is an automorphism, so their units have the same kernel. Invertibility supplies quasi-coherence through the source-library instance IsInvertible.isQuasicoherent.

Write m as the supremum of the principal ideals (a), indexed by all a in m, including zero. These ideals are directed because ideals of a valuation ring are totally ordered. Ideal extension and ideal multiplication on a module commute with suprema (Mathlib Ideal.map_iSup and Submodule.iSup_smul). Submodule.mem_iSup_of_directed therefore shows that each affine restriction of s, which lies in m Gamma(U,L), already lies in (a_U) Gamma(U,L) for some a_U in m. These are algebraic span and directed-union calculations, implemented by the proved private helper exists_principal_stage.

Quasi-compactness of f over the affine base makes X compact; select a finite affine subcover using Mathlib isCompact_univ.elim_finite_subcover. Since A is not a field, IsLocalRing.isField_iff_maximalIdeal_eq and Submodule.exists_mem_ne_zero_of_ne_bot give a nonzero a_0 in m. Inductively compare the principal ideals of the finitely many a_U and a_0. Total ordering gives a principal ideal (pi) containing all of them, with pi in m. Its containing a_0 forces pi nonzero. The private helper finite_principal_upper_bound proves the finite induction.

For every affine open in the chosen finite cover, extension preserves (a_U) <= (pi), so its restricted section lies in (pi) Gamma(U,L). Apply the affine kernel criterion from step 1 in the reverse direction. Naturality of the pullback unit identifies these zero sections with restrictions of the global image of s. The sheaf uniqueness axiom, Mathlib TopCat.Sheaf.eq_of_locally_eq', makes this global image zero. This is the required vanishing modulo pi.

lean.statement: theorem exists_nonzero_maximalIdeal_section_eq_zero (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [ValuationRing A] (hA : ¬ IsField A) {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of A)) [LocallyOfFinitePresentation f] [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] (L : X.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (s : L.val.obj (op ⊤)) (hs : ((Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A))))))).unit.app L).val.app (op ⊤) s = 0) : ∃ π : A, π ≠ 0 ∧ π ∈ IsLocalRing.maximalIdeal A ∧ ((Classical.choose (exists_tensorPullbackAdjunction (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span {π}))))))).unit.app L).val.app (op ⊤) s = 0
